originalTitle: Romell Glave soars to European men’s 100m title in British one-two ahead of Jeremiah Azu
summary: Britain’s Romell Glave won a stunning gold in the men’s 100m at the European championships, with his teammate Jeremiah Azu picking up silver
content: On Marcell Jacobs’ right arm there is a tattoo of the Roman colosseum and a gladiator: a reminder of his fighting spirit and what Italy’s capital means to him. But in the swirling bearpit of a European championships 100m final, the former Olympic champion’s body dramatically broke down. That was the first shock. The second was the sight of two Britons, Romell Glave and Jeremiah Azu, blasting through to take gold and silver. True, their finishing times were nothing special. But tell that to the 16,000 crowd who cheered to the rafters as Glave took gold in a modest 10.09sec, with Azu following him home in 10.16. Germany’s Owen Ansah claimed bronze in 10.19. And Jacobs? Well, he looked a little saddened and weary as he hobbled over the line in 12.26. “It doesn’t really matter about the time,” said Glave, who was wearing sunglasses and certainly left his rivals in the shade. “The condition wasn’t as great because of the headwind. But I wasn’t really focused on that. I was focused on my race. I was able to do that today and I’m king of the world.” This was the third time Britain has won gold and silver in the men’s 100m at the European championships, following Darren Campbell beating Dwain Chambers in 1998 and Zharnel Hughes finishing ahead of Reece Prescod in 2018. Yet few would have put their money on it happening again when Jacobs, the twice European 100m champion who also won gold in the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, looked so imperious when strolling through his semi-final in 10.08. But shortly after the gun went off in the final, everyone’s assumptions were shot to pieces as Azu set a searing pace, Glave followed – and the Italian’s injury-ridden body suddenly broke down. “I was ahead, so I wasn’t really sure what happened until I saw the replay,” said Glave. “That’s when I realised that he pulled up.” Afterwards, as he sported a crown on his head, he explained that he had moved from Jamaica to London at 15 in search of a better life. “I came over to live with my family,” he said. My dad was over here, and there’s more opportunity in Britain compared to Jamaica. “There’s a more opportunity to join an athletics club,” he added. “And that resource that he gave me, I’m like a living testimony. Just standing here to show that I was born in Jamaica, but Britain is where I was made.” Asked about wearing sunglasses late at night, Glave said he had decided to do it this year. “It’s a part of my style, it is a part of my personality and fashion identity. It’s a new thing for this year because this year means business.” That business of sprinting has not always been smooth, though. Glave was the world’s fastest teenager in 2017, when he ran 10.21 as a 17-year-old. But his back was in a brace for the whole of 2022. And he was unable to build on a European bronze medal in 2024 after what he says was a fracture in his back that became inflamed. But the 26-year-old has been working on his sprint mechanics with his coach Michael Afilaka – and this was his just reward. Azu, meanwhile, was happy enough with silver after an up and down season. “Normally, I’m quite consistent,” he said. “This year, it’s been one race great, the next not: up and down. But when it comes to championships, I know I find my best, and I showed that today.” There was at least an Italian success in the women’s 5,000m as Nadia Battocletti obliterated the field in the final 200m. “The race was super-tactical, but then I played my winning card,” said Battocletti, who won a slowly run race in 15:37.84. Spain’s Marta García took silver, more than two seconds back, with another Italian, Micol Majori, winning bronze. But there was disappointment for Britain’s Hannah Nuttall, who slipped to fifth after being in a prominent position at the bell. In the women’s 100m hurdles final, Nadine Visser of the Netherlands took gold by one-thousandth of a second to defeat Poland’s Pia Skrzyszowska. Both women finished with a time of 12.67 but after a long time to assess the photo-finish, Visser was given the award. “I won the dip from Pia and that doesn’t happen very often,” she said. Elsewhere the Olympic long jump champion Miltiadis Tentoglou of Greece won his fourth European title with a leap of 8.44m, while Simon Ehammer of Switzerland took silver after jumping 8.29m.
chineseTitle: 罗梅尔·格拉夫 (Romell Glave) 在英国一对二比赛中领先杰里米亚·阿祖 (Jeremiah Azu) 夺得欧洲男子 100 米冠军
chineseSummary: 英国选手罗梅尔·格拉夫 (Romell Glave) 在欧洲锦标赛男子 100 米比赛中夺得金牌，他的队友耶利米·阿祖 (Jeremiah Azu) 摘得银牌
chineseContent: 马塞尔·雅各布斯的右臂上有罗马斗兽场和角斗士的纹身：提醒着他的战斗精神以及意大利首都对他的意义。但在欧洲锦标赛 100 米决赛的漩涡熊坑中，这位前奥运冠军的身体急剧崩溃。这是第一次震惊。第二个是两个英国人罗梅尔·格拉夫和耶利米·阿祖的景象，他们冲过去夺取金银。确实，他们的完成时间并没有什么特别的。但请告诉 16,000 名在椽子上欢呼的观众，格拉夫仅用了 10.09 秒就获得了金牌，阿祖则以 10.16 秒的成绩追随他回家。德国选手欧文·安萨 (Owen Ansah) 在 10.19 中获得铜牌。雅各布斯呢？好吧，当他以 12.26 的成绩一瘸一拐地冲过终点线时，他看起来有点悲伤和疲惫。 “时间并不重要，”戴着墨镜的格拉夫说，他的对手们显然都被远远甩在了后面。 “由于逆风，情况不太好。但我并没有真正专注于此。我专注于我的比赛。今天我能够做到这一点，我是世界之王。”这是英国第三次在欧洲锦标赛上获得男子 100 米金牌和银牌，此前达伦·坎贝尔 (Darren Campbell) 在 1998 年击败了德温·钱伯斯 (Dwain Chambers)，扎内尔·休斯 (Zharnel Hughes) 在 2018 年领先里斯·普雷斯科德 (Reece Prescod)。然而，当两届欧洲 100 米冠军、也在 2020 年东京奥运会上夺得金牌的雅各布斯 (Jacobs) 漫步在自己的家中时，他显得如此傲慢，很少有人会认为这样的事情会再次发生。 10.08 半决赛。但决赛枪响后不久，随着阿祖加快步伐，格拉夫紧随其后，所有人的假设都被击碎了——意大利人饱受伤病的身体突然崩溃了。 “我领先了，所以在看到重播之前我不太确定发生了什么，”格拉夫说。 “那时我才意识到
